Prepare all consumer form values (name, callback URL, permission set)
Advise the minimal scope string set for authorize requests

approval.trigger: No review of any kind for OAuth consumers: nothing in the documentation describes an Atlassian approval, submission, or vetting step before real users can connect. Create the consumer, share the authorize URL, and each user personally consents. There is no marketplace or listing for OAuth consumers (Marketplace listing exists only for Forge/Connect apps, a different mechanism; new Bitbucket Connect apps can no longer be registered as of February 2, 2026).

blockers.detail: Both grants return a refresh token, and refreshing issues a NEW one (the old expires shortly after and 'should not be used again'). But 'a refresh token which is not used to generate an access token will expire after 3 months', after which the user must complete the full authorization flow again. Inactive users disconnect silently at the 3-month mark.
blockers.howToClear: Persist the replacement refresh token on every refresh, and schedule periodic refreshes (or graceful re-authorization prompts) for dormant connections.
blockers.title: Refresh tokens expire after 3 months unused

blockers.detail: Enforced changes from the developer changelog (May 4, 2026): access tokens are accepted ONLY as Bearer tokens in the Authorization header to api.bitbucket.org (query-string and POST-body tokens are rejected); token responses return 'scope' instead of 'scopes'; client credentials grants no longer issue refresh tokens. Older integrations and tutorials built on query-string tokens break.
blockers.howToClear: Send tokens only in the Authorization header and audit any legacy code paths before they fail in production.
blockers.title: May 2026 breaking auth changes

blockers.detail: If you include a callback URL in a request, 'it must be appended to the same URL configured in the consumer' (consumer example.com/add-on permits request example.com/add-on/function). If omitted, Bitbucket redirects to the configured callback URL. Free-form redirect URIs from other providers' mental models will not work.
blockers.howToClear: Configure the base callback URL on the consumer and append paths beneath it.
blockers.title: Callback URL must extend the configured URL

flavor.recommended: An OAuth consumer in your own Bitbucket workspace, using the 3-LO (authorization code) flow
flavor.why: 'OAuth needs a key and secret; together these are known as an OAuth consumer.' The consumer's Key is the client_id and its Secret the client_secret. End users authorize via bitbucket.org/site/oauth2/authorize and the token acts on behalf of the authorizing user. (Bitbucket's OAuth 2 grew out of its OAuth 1 system: existing OAuth 1 consumers automatically became valid OAuth 2 clients once a callback URL was configured.)

humanMust: Create the consumer in a workspace you administer and copy the Key and Secret
Choose the permission set on the consumer
End users consent in the OAuth dialog
name: Bitbucket
nuances: Access tokens expire in one hour; on expiry you get 401 responses. Refresh is mandatory for any long-lived agent connection.

The 'repository' scope does not give access to a repository's pull requests; PR access needs its own scopes (pullrequest, pullrequest:write). Over-asking has a cost too: a descriptor lacking scopes is implicitly assumed to require all scopes (Connect context).
Implicit Grant and Resource Owner Password Credentials are no longer supported per the developer docs, though an Atlassian support page still documents the implicit flow; older tutorials mislead.
Access tokens can clone over HTTPS as https://x-token-auth:{access_token}@bitbucket.org/... (the literal username 'x-token-auth' is required).
Consumers are not listed or discoverable anywhere; distribution is entirely 'send users your authorize URL'.
prerequisites: Your permission set (form checkboxes and authorize-time scope strings)

steps.detail: Workspace settings > Apps and features > OAuth consumers > Add consumer. Fields: Name (required, unique within your account), optional Description, Callback URL (required for OAuth 2.0), optional URL, the 'This is a private consumer' checkbox, and Permissions checkboxes by area (Account, Repositories, Pull requests, etc.).
steps.title: Add an OAuth consumer

steps.detail: Save; expand the consumer name to view the Key (client_id) and Secret (client_secret). Copy and vault the Secret.
steps.title: Copy the Key and Secret

steps.detail: Send users to bitbucket.org/site/oauth2/authorize?client_id={client_id}&response_type=code. Exchange the returned code at bitbucket.org/site/oauth2/access_token with HTTP Basic client_id:secret and grant_type=authorization_code. Call api.bitbucket.org/2.0 with Authorization: Bearer {access_token} (header only, since the May 2026 enforcement).
steps.title: Implement the 3-LO flow

steps.detail: Access tokens live one hour. Refresh before expiry; store the NEW refresh token every time (the old one expires shortly after use), and never let a refresh token sit unused for 3 months or the user must re-authorize from scratch.
steps.title: Handle refresh rotation and the 3-month clock

tagline: An 'OAuth consumer' on your workspace plus a standard authorization-code flow, with no review and no listing anywhere. The traps are in the token lifecycle: one-hour access tokens, rotating refresh tokens, and a 3-month use-it-or-lose-it expiry.

time.active: ~5 min of console work + ~1 hr of flow code
time.total: Same day; usable the moment the consumer is saved
